title: What school used to be like, with the imperfect

tips.title: Nous form, drop -ons, add the endings
tips.body: *Nous jou**ons*** → *jou-* → *je jou**ais***. Take the **nous** form of the present, cut *-ons*, and add **-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient**. That one rule builds the imperfect of every verb in French — with a single exception, and one spelling point: before *i*, *-ger* verbs drop the *e* and *-cer* verbs turn *ç* into *c* (*nous mangions, nous commencions*).

tips.title: Être is the only irregular stem
tips.body: *Nous sommes* does not end in *-ons*, so *être* takes the stem **ét-**: *j'**ét**ais, tu étais, il était, nous étions, vous étiez, ils étaient.* Learn that one and you have them all — *avoir* is regular (*nous avons* → *av-* → *j'avais*).

tips.title: Used to, was …-ing, or a description
tips.body: The imperfect covers three English shapes: *je jouais* = **I used to play**, **I was playing**, or simply **I played** when describing a habit. If the English has *used to* or *was …-ing*, the French is the imperfect.

tips.title: Imperfect for the background, perfect for the event
tips.body: *Je **regardais** la télé quand le téléphone **a sonné**.* The imperfect sets the scene that was already going on; the perfect drops the single event into it. *Quand* usually sits between the two.

tips.title: Avant, quand j'étais petit(e)
tips.body: *Avant, à l'école primaire, on **finissait** à trois heures.* *Quand j'**étais** petit(e), je **détestais** la lecture.* Two openings that announce the imperfect before the verb arrives, and both fit any "what was it like" question.

why.matters: *What was primary school like?* needs a tense for how things were, and the imperfect is the easiest one in French to build: the *nous* form of the present with *-ons* cut off, six endings, and *être* as the only exception. The topic exists because the imperfect is one of the three time frames the exam counts, because it describes the background against which perfect-tense events happen, and because *quand j'étais petit* is the opening of half the writing tasks you will ever be set.

examples.title: Nous form, drop -ons, add the endings
examples.body: *Faire* is irregular in the present and perfectly regular here, because the *nous* form already contains the irregularity: *nous faisons* gives *fais-*, and the endings do the rest. The picture shows why the tense is quick: one stem, six endings, and the first three sound the same so the spelling is the mark. *Être* alone invents a stem, *ét-*; everything else, however strange in the present, follows this table.

visual.alt: A conjugation table of faire in the imperfect with the stem fais, from nous faisons, drawn apart from the endings ais, ais, ait, ions, iez and aient

examples.title: Three jobs for one tense
examples.body: English needs three phrases for what the French imperfect does alone: *I used to play*, *I was playing*, and *it was small*. A habit, an action in progress, a description, all *je jouais* or *c'était*. The marker words tell you which is meant, *avant* and *tous les jours* for the habit, *quand* for the interrupted action, and a reading text about someone's childhood is the imperfect from start to finish.

examples.title: The phone rang while I was watching
examples.body: The imperfect and the perfect work as a pair: *je regardais la télé quand le téléphone a sonné*. The watching is the background, long and unfinished, so it is imperfect; the ringing is a single event, so it is perfect. Every story has both, and the exam listens for the switch. *Comme j'étais malade, je ne suis pas allé à l'école* is the same pair with a reason in front.

steps.title: Former l'imparfait
steps.body:
The imperfect is the easiest French tense to build, because there is **one rule and one exception**.

**The rule**: take the **nous** form of the present tense, cut off **-ons**, and add the imperfect endings.

*Nous **jouons*** → *jou-* → *je **jouais**.* *Nous **finissons*** → *finiss-* → *je **finissais**.* *Nous **faisons*** → *fais-* → *je **faisais**.* *Nous **prenons*** → *pren-* → *je **prenais**.* *Nous **buvons*** → *buv-* → *je **buvais**.*

This works for verbs that are irregular in the present — *faire, prendre, boire, aller* (*nous allons* → *j'allais*) — because the *nous* form already contains their irregularity.

**The endings**: *-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient*. The first three and the last one all sound the same.

**The exception**: ***être***. *Nous sommes* has no *-ons*, so the stem is **ét-**: *j'étais, tu étais, il/elle/on était, nous étions, vous étiez, ils/elles étaient.*

**Avoir is regular**: *nous avons* → *av-* → *j'avais, tu avais, il avait, nous avions, vous aviez, ils avaient*.

**One spelling point**: *-ger* and *-cer* verbs keep the *e* or *ç* of the *nous* form only before *a*: *je mangeais, je commençais*, but *nous mangions, vous commenciez*.

On the Pearson specification the imperfect is needed at both tiers for *je, tu* and *il / elle / on*; the plural forms (*nous, vous, ils / elles*) are Higher tier only.

steps.title: Quand l'utiliser
steps.body:
The imperfect covers three jobs, and all three turn up in a "what school was like" answer.

**1. A habit in the past — *used to***: *quand j'étais à l'école primaire, on **finissait** à trois heures*. *Tous les jours, je **prenais** le bus.*

**2. A description in the past — *was / were***: *l'école **était** petite*, *il y **avait** trente élèves*, *les profs **étaient** sévères*, *c'**était** génial*.

**3. An action in progress — *was …-ing***: *je **faisais** mes devoirs quand ma mère est rentrée*.

**Against the perfect**: the perfect is for a **single completed event**. Compare:

- *Je **jouais** au foot tous les samedis* (habit — imperfect)
- *Samedi dernier, j'**ai joué** au foot* (one event — perfect)
- *Je **jouais** au foot **quand** je **suis tombé*** (background + event)

**Markers for the imperfect**: *avant, autrefois* (in the past), *quand j'étais petit(e), à l'époque* (at the time), *tous les jours, chaque semaine, d'habitude, souvent, toujours*.

**Markers for the perfect**: *un jour, soudain* (suddenly), *hier, samedi dernier, une fois*.

steps.title: L'imparfait et le passé composé ensemble
steps.body:
The two past tenses do **different jobs**, and a strong answer uses both in the same sentence.

**The background is imperfect, the event is perfect**:

*Je **regardais** la télé **quand** le téléphone **a sonné**.* (I was watching TV when the phone rang.)
*Il **faisait** beau, donc on **est allés** au parc.* (It was fine, so we went to the park.)
*Comme j'**étais** malade, je **n'ai pas** passé le contrôle.* (As I was ill, I did not sit the test.)

**Think of it as a stage**: the imperfect paints the set — the weather, the time, how people felt, what was already happening. The perfect is what walks on and happens.

**Setting a scene**: *il **faisait** froid, il **était** huit heures, j'**avais** peur* (I was afraid), *tout le monde **attendait***, *je **ne savais pas** quoi faire* (I did not know what to do).

**Three time frames in one answer**: *avant, on **finissait** à quinze heures* (imperfect) · *l'année dernière, j'**ai changé** d'école* (perfect) · *maintenant, je **finis** à dix-sept heures* (present). 15h to 17h is 2 hours later.

**Comparing then and now**: *avant … maintenant …*, *c'était mieux avant* (it was better before), *les choses ont changé* (things have changed), *à l'époque* (at the time).

steps.title: Your turn
steps.body:
**Part A.**

1. Write the six imperfect endings.
2. Build the imperfect stem of *jouer, finir, faire, prendre, aller*.
3. Write the six forms of *être* in the imperfect.

**Part B.**

4. Write three things you used to do at primary school.
5. Describe your primary school with *était* and *il y avait*.
6. Write *I was watching TV when the phone rang.*

**Part C.**

7. Write a sentence with *comme j'étais …, je n'ai pas …*
8. Compare then and now with *avant … maintenant …*
9. Write six sentences about primary school: three habits, one description, one single event in the perfect, and a comparison with now.

For question 9, check each verb: habit or description is imperfect, a one-off event is perfect.

steps.title: Going deeper
steps.body:
**Build the stem from the nous form, every time.** *Nous buvons* → *je buvais*; *nous prenons* → *je prenais*. Verbs that look irregular in the present are regular here, and knowing that is what makes the tense quick.

**Être is the only exception.** *J'étais, nous étions.* If you find yourself inventing another irregular stem, you are wrong.

**Watch nous and vous of -ier and -yer verbs.** *Nous étudions* → *nous étudi**ions***, *vous essay**iez***. The *i* of the stem and the *i* of the ending both stay.

**And before i, -ger verbs drop their e and -cer verbs turn ç into c.** *Je mangeais* but *nous mangions*; *je commençais* but *vous commenciez*.

**Choose the tense by the job, not by the English word.** *I played every Saturday* is a habit, so *je jouais*, even though English gives no *used to*.

**Pair the two past tenses.** *Je faisais mes devoirs quand il est arrivé.* One sentence containing both is the clearest evidence that you know the difference.

**Use comme and donc.** *Comme il pleuvait, on est restés à l'intérieur.* *Il faisait froid, donc j'ai mis un manteau.* A causal link between a background and an event reads as mature French.

**Keep c'était for the judgement.** *C'était génial, c'était dur, c'était mieux avant.* It is an imperfect and it belongs with the description.

**Then three time frames.** Imperfect for what it was like, perfect for what happened, present for now — and, if you can, a near future for next year. That is the full range in one paragraph.

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- **Stem**: the **nous** form of the present, minus **-ons**.
- **Endings**: *-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient*.
- *Nous jouons → je jouais; nous faisons → je faisais; nous prenons → je prenais; nous allons → j'allais.*
- **Être** is the only exception: stem **ét-** — *j'étais, nous étions*.
- *Avoir* is regular: *nous avons → j'avais*.
- **Three jobs**: a habit (*used to*), a description (*was / were*), an action in progress (*was …-ing*).
- **Perfect** for a single completed event.
- *Je regardais la télé **quand** le téléphone **a sonné**.*
- Imperfect markers: *avant, autrefois, quand j'étais petit(e), à l'époque, tous les jours, souvent*.
- Perfect markers: *un jour, soudain, hier, une fois*.
- *Il y **avait**, c'**était**, il **faisait** beau, je **ne savais pas***.
- *Comme j'étais malade, je n'ai pas …*
- Compare: *avant … maintenant …*, *c'était mieux avant*.
- *-ier* verbs keep both *i*: *nous étudiions*.
- *-ger* / *-cer* verbs: *je mangeais* but *nous mangions*.

examTechnique.body:
Build the imperfect from the **nous** form minus **-ons**, plus *-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient*; **être** (*ét-*) is the only exception.

Use it for **habits**, **descriptions** and **actions in progress**, and the perfect for a **single event** — then pair them in one sentence with *quand* or *comme*. Judge with *c'était*, and compare *avant* with *maintenant* to show three time frames.
examinerErrors: Building the stem from the infinitive instead of the nous form.
Inventing an irregular stem other than ét-.
The perfect for a repeated habit.
The imperfect for a one-off event.
Dropping an i in nous étudiions.
Keeping des or une after a negative.
Only one past tense in the whole answer.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer builds every imperfect from the *nous* form without hesitation, knows *ét-* is the only exception, and chooses between the two past tenses by the job each does. It pairs them inside one sentence with *quand* or *comme*, sets a scene with *il y avait*, *il faisait* and *je ne savais pas*, judges with *c'était*, keeps both letters in *nous étudiions*, and ends by putting *avant*, a single past event, and *maintenant* side by side.
